text:
Priya (CSM): Meridian go-live next Tue. Customer asked for an SLO acceptance packet: uptime, p95 latency, and a worked credit example. Can SRE/Eng help draft?
Liam (SRE): I can pull 30d availability and flag any spikes >0.2%. How does customer define downtime?
Priya (CSM): Legal says service count as unavailable when availability < target for >=5m. Latency p95 measured per UTC day per route.
Jordan (Eng): We'll export p95 per route + per-region. Also add a note on fallback routing behavior.
Sam (Enablement): I will draft a one-pager and FAQ. Include a worked example for a 30-day billing period.
Alex (Support): Add a short warm-start checklist for latency spikes and an ops contact.
ops-bot: KB link added: https://console.redwood.com/kb/latency-warmup
Liam (SRE): Plan: run simplified uptime query, export CSVs, annotate timezone handling, and include a short RCA for any dips. ETA today.
Jordan (Eng): I'll produce p95 JSON and a small trace screenshot for an outlier. Note: fallback replica can add ~30-50ms tail.
Priya (CSM): Legal wants a worked credit example if monthly availability is 99.2 vs 99.5 target. Bizops to confirm cap.
Sam (Enablement): Draft wording: "credits proportional to minutes below target, capped at Y%" — will leave cap placeholder.
Alex (Support): I'll run the 30m walkthrough during customer briefing and capture action items.
Priya (CSM): Timeline: draft pack by EOD tomorrow, briefing Thu. Please drop artifacts in onboarding evidence folder when ready.
Liam (SRE): Will flag 2024-01-12 us-west dip (0.4% for ~12m) in the export.
Jordan (Eng): I'll add a blurb explaining how fallback affects latency metrics.
Priya (CSM): Thanks team — I'll assemble the customer-facing package once artifacts are in the folder. :rocket:
